details: The European Central Bank (ECB) raised its key deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.5% on Thursday, its second hike this year. President Christine Lagarde stated that inflation in the eurozone is proving more persistent than anticipated, largely due to ongoing volatility in energy prices driven by the Middle East conflict. The ECB also revised up its growth forecasts for 2026 and 2027, noting the economy's resilience, but signalled potential for further tightening to bring inflation back to its 2% target.
title: ECB Raises Rates to 2.5%, Warns of Prolonged Eurozone Inflation

details: Kristalina Georgieva, head of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), warned that the global economy could face a "much worse outcome" if the Middle East war extends into 2027, potentially pushing oil prices to around $125 per barrel. This scenario would lead to climbing inflation and a significant slowdown in global growth. The IMF is expected to downgrade its economic growth forecasts, highlighting concerns over geopolitical tensions and their impact on supply chains and energy costs.
title: IMF Chief Warns of Slower Growth and Higher Inflation from Middle East War

details: Recent U.S. inflation data revealed that annual headline inflation rose to 3.4% in August, reinforcing market expectations that the Federal Reserve might raise interest rates at its upcoming September meeting. This prospect of tighter monetary policy is adding macroeconomic pressure and uncertainty to risk-sensitive assets, including Bitcoin, which has seen renewed pressure and volatility in its price.
title: August US Inflation Data Boosts Fed Hike Expectations, Weighs on Bitcoin

details: Finance ministers and central bank governors from BRICS nations concluded their summit by calling for reforms to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank to enhance the influence of developing and emerging economies. They also announced plans to accelerate efforts on cross-border payments and expand trade settlements in national currencies, aiming for more efficient, secure, and accessible transactions.
title: BRICS Advocates for Global Financial Reforms and National Currency Settlements
